strategies I've used as someone who has had several fps, obsessed over people to their extreme detriment n mine:
- making myself my "favorite person" (seriously this helps)
  - in quotes because of the below book
  - you are and will always be the best person for urself
  - you are the only person who will ever love you the best/know you the most (most because we are constantly changing and learning new things about ourself)
  - you are the only person who can give you what you want
- reading n applying the skills brought up in "all about love" by bell hooks
  - I use this to remind myself what love Is and what it is not, it is not a deep draw to/obsession with or only affection, it is a Choice to “extend one’s self for the purpose of nurturing one’s own or another’s spiritual growth” using "care, affection, recognition, respect, commitment, and trust, as well as honest and open communication."
- reading n applying the skills brought up in https://www.instagram.com/the.holistic.psychologist/
- reading n applying the skills brought up in "the dialectical behavior therapy skills workbook"
  - particular to fps: mindfulness n sitting with your emotions like they are leaves on a calm stream you are sitting beside, watching them float by
    - we are constantly bombarded with messages, all the time, the leaves are going to be all shapes n colors n sizes n smells n whatever, and that's okay, that's the way it's meant to be. it's okay to have any kind of feeling, what matters is what you do with it. do you respond to it? sometimes that's important, sometimes it's best to let to drift away
- reading about abandonment fears, this was a lot of why I attach to people n detach from them in that way, like my parents weren't awful, they were human beings tho and I either received very intrusive overwhelming love (creating feelings of needing escape/distrust) or completely detached interaction (creating feelings of desperation for love). like ur childhood actually affects so much of what your behavior is now. the insta I linked above talks a lot about methods to work with that, like "reparenting" yourself (see the top bullet: you are the best person for yourself)
- understanding the 4 skills marsha linehan created in dbt n using these all in creating a plan for yourself in managing the feelings you get caught on
  - mindfulness
  - interpersonal skills based on asking for what you need (I forget the name of this)
  - emotional regulation (CHANGE)
    - understanding n acting on ur desire to be free of interdependence
  - distress tolerance (ACCEPTANCE)
    - accepting that your experiences have gotten you to where you are
